conceptCards.title: Array types, tuple types, and readonly tuples
conceptCards.summary: Array types, tuple types, and readonly tuples covers built-in data structures and iteration protocols.

conceptCards.title: Typing Map, Set, and Weak collections
conceptCards.summary: Map<K,V> and Set<T> are ES2015 collections with generic type parameters — unlike plain objects, they accept any key type and preserve insertion order.

conceptCards.title: The satisfies operator and type-preserving literals
conceptCards.summary: The satisfies operator and type-preserving literals is where JavaScript dynamic typing surprises C# developers — implicit ToNumber, ToString, and truthiness rules that === and O...

conceptCards.title: ReadonlyArray, ReadonlySet, and immutable views
conceptCards.summary: readonly T[] and ReadonlyArray<T> block mutating methods at compile time — but the underlying array is still mutable at runtime if another reference exists.

conceptCards.title: Typing map/filter/reduce callbacks precisely
conceptCards.summary: Array.map, filter, and reduce infer callback parameter types from the array element type — but generic pipelines, tuple returns, and reduce accumulators need explicit type param...

conceptCards.title: TypeScript collections versus C# generics collections
conceptCards.summary: TypeScript arrays and Map/Set erase at compile time — C# List<T> and Dictionary<K,V> enforce generics at runtime through the CLR.
